readings: Outputs are registered (Moore machine): a change in s is captured on the clock edge, and fr2/fr1/fr0/dfr update on the following cycle.
Outputs are combinational (Mealy machine): fr2/fr1/fr0/dfr respond to s in the same cycle, with no additional register delay.
The previous-level register updates only when s changes, so dfr stays asserted while the level remains in a higher middle interval until the next sensor change.
The previous-level register updates every clock, so dfr is asserted only for the one cycle immediately following a rising transition and deasserts on the next cycle even if s is unchanged.
Invalid s values (e.g., 010, 100, 101, 110) are treated as don't cares; the FSM holds its current state and outputs.
Invalid s values are decoded as the nearest valid level (e.g., 010 as between s[1] and s[0]) or cause a transition to the reset state, changing outputs.
